version.changelog: Full coverage pass: deeper guides, situation-named files, and per-user configuration

llm.summary: This is a coherent Playwright helper skill with disclosed browser automation, session, and CI artifact risks that users should handle carefully.

dimensions.detail: Node, npx, browser downloads, repository access, site interaction, Docker flags, and CI report uploads are proportionate for Playwright work, but reports, traces, HARs, and storage state can contain sensitive data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Install metadata and examples use npm/npx for playwright and @playwright/mcp without exact package versions; this is purpose-aligned but leaves a mutable supply-chain dependency users should pin in sensitive environments.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions scope automation to user-requested sites and flows, default away from production or destructive actions, and explicitly warn that page text is untrusted data rather than agent instruction.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill stores only preferences and observations under ~/Clawic/data/playwright/ and explicitly excludes credentials there; persistent browser profiles and storageState files are optional and described as credential-bearing.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's Playwright testing, browser automation, MCP control, CI debugging, auth-state handling, and rendered-page extraction capabilities match its stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, pin Playwright and MCP package versions or use a project lockfile, prefer isolated browser profiles for credentialed work, keep .auth files, traces, HARs, and videos out of git and shared storage, restrict CI artifact access and retention, and require explicit approval before automating production, paid, or destructive flows.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced migration.md file is present and was inspected; it contains Playwright migration guidance, not analysis evasion behavior.
[YR4] expected: The flagged phrase appears inside defensive guidance telling agents to treat hostile page text as data, not as instructions.
[P1] expected: The instruction-override wording is an example of an attack shown in a warning, not an instruction issued by the skill.
[PE5] expected: The --ipc=host Docker advice is a Playwright/Chromium stability workaround and is accompanied by less broad alternatives; users should prefer narrower container settings when possible.
[RA2] expected: Storage-state and browser profile persistence are normal Playwright auth workflows, and the artifact repeatedly warns to gitignore them, avoid shared folders, and avoid production credentials.
[RP1] expected: The many npx examples are normal Playwright CLI usage, but unpinned package execution should be replaced with lockfile-controlled or version-pinned commands where supply-chain control matters.
[T08] expected: The unpinned npm package concern is valid as a supply-chain caution, but installing Playwright/MCP is disclosed and central to the skill's function.
[T09] expected: CI artifact upload supports debugging and is disclosed with short retention, but users should restrict access and avoid uploading reports that contain tokens, cookies, or personal data.
[html-comment-injection] expected: The HTML comments found are placeholders inside a fenced memory template and do not contain hidden runtime instructions.
